sops.title: Zone Temperature Below Profile Setpoint
sops.condition: One or more zone thermocouples read 5–15°C below the configured reflow profile setpoint during an active production run.

sops.title: Zone Temperature Sudden Collapse
sops.condition: Any zone thermocouple drops more than 25°C within a 60-second window, indicating a probable heater element failure.

sops.title: Zone Temperature Above Upper Ceiling Limit
sops.condition: Any zone thermocouple exceeds the configured upper ceiling temperature limit, activating an over-temperature alarm.

sops.title: Conveyor Speed Below Programmed Setpoint
sops.condition: The conveyor belt speed sensor reads more than 10% below the programmed profile setpoint for a continuous period exceeding 30 seconds, while the belt remains in motion.

sops.title: Conveyor Motion Complete Stop During Run
sops.condition: The conveyor motion sensor reads zero belt movement while the oven is in active production mode with boards loaded.

sops.title: PCB Jam at Oven Entry Zone
sops.condition: The entry zone board-present sensor remains continuously blocked for more than 30 seconds during a production run.

sops.title: PCB Jam at Oven Exit or Cooling Zone
sops.condition: The exit or cooling zone board-present sensor remains continuously blocked for more than 30 seconds while boards are in process.

sops.title: Exhaust Airflow Below Advisory Warning Threshold
sops.condition: The exhaust duct airflow sensor drops below the minimum advisory warning threshold, triggering a non-critical alarm on the control panel while oven remains operational.

sops.title: Exhaust Airflow Critical Failure Emergency
sops.condition: The exhaust duct airflow sensor reads near-zero, indicating complete fan failure or fully blocked ductwork, creating an immediate fume accumulation hazard requiring immediate shutdown.

sops.title: Nitrogen Supply Pressure Below Minimum Setpoint
sops.condition: The nitrogen supply pressure sensor reads below the minimum setpoint required to maintain an inert atmosphere in the reflow tunnel.

sops.title: Cooling Zone Exceeds Maximum Exit Temperature
sops.condition: The cooling zone thermocouple reads above the maximum permissible board exit temperature limit, risking thermal damage to assembled components.

sops.title: Heater Zone Electrical or Ground Fault Alarm
sops.condition: A heater zone SCR driver or ground fault alarm activates on the control panel display during oven operation.

sops.title: Scheduled Conveyor Chain Lubrication
sops.condition: The preventive maintenance calendar indicates the scheduled conveyor chain lubrication interval has elapsed.

sops.title: Exhaust Flux Filter Replacement
sops.condition: The exhaust filter differential pressure gauge reaches the change-required limit or the scheduled replacement interval elapses on the maintenance calendar.

sops.title: Zone Thermocouple Calibration Verification
sops.condition: The periodic calibration schedule is due or a zone thermocouple drift exceeding ±2°C relative to the reference standard is detected.

sops.title: Scheduled Conveyor Belt Tension and Wear Inspection
sops.condition: The preventive maintenance calendar indicates the conveyor belt tension and wear inspection interval has been reached.

sops.title: Nitrogen Flow Meter Sensor Scheduled Cleaning
sops.condition: The scheduled nitrogen flow meter sensor cleaning interval has elapsed per the preventive maintenance calendar.

sops.title: Cooling Zone Fan Blade Cleaning
sops.condition: The scheduled cooling zone fan blade cleaning interval has elapsed or visual inspection reveals significant flux residue accumulation on fan blades.

sops.title: Reflow Oven Lockout Tagout Procedure
sops.condition: A maintenance task requiring physical access inside the reflow oven enclosure is scheduled to begin.

sops.title: Minor Flux Residue Spill Response
sops.condition: A flux residue spill of less than one liter is observed on the oven exterior surface or immediately adjacent floor area.

sops.title: Major Flux Container Rupture and Spill Response
sops.condition: A flux container failure or rupture releases more than five liters of flux in or around the oven area, creating an immediate chemical exposure hazard.

sops.title: Reflow Oven Cold Start Startup Procedure
sops.condition: The reflow oven is in a fully de-energized and cold state and requires startup for production.

incidents.text: Line 3 reflow unit had zone 2 reading low all morning — sitting about 8 degrees under where it should be for the profile we're running. Product was still moving but I'm watching it. Waited a couple minutes and it pulled itself back into tolerance.
Second shift flagged zone 4 on the unit by the loading dock — it was trailing cold by maybe 10 degrees, boards still running through. Nothing drastic, just not hitting its number.
Zone 1 was reading shy of target during the afternoon run on line 2 — roughly 12 degrees low, gradual drift, belt was still rolling the whole time. Kept checking it every few minutes.
Zone 3 just fell off a cliff — display went from 240 down to 205 in maybe 45 seconds. Nothing gradual about it, total loss. Heater's definitely gone on line 1.
Was watching the profile trace on the unit near tooling storage and zone 5 cratered — dropped 30 degrees in under a minute. Went from setpoint to way below in no time flat.
Zone 2 tanked hard right at the start of the afternoon run. Reading was fine and then suddenly it was 28 below. Not a slow drift — it just quit. Looks like the heater element died.
Zone 4 overtemp alarm went off during the run on line 3 — display was showing way past the max mark, alarm was screaming. Had to stop the belt right away.
Zone 1 was cooking hot — alarm lit and the reading was above the red line on the gauge. Boards were still on the belt when the alarm hit.
Got an overtemp on zone 3 during first shift, reading was 18 degrees past the ceiling limit. Alarm was going off and the number just kept climbing.

Belt on the line 2 oven was dragging — not stopped, but definitely slow. Boards were taking longer to come out than the recipe calls for. Looked at the readout and it was running about 12% under the programmed speed.
Speed was low all of first shift, maybe 15% below the setting. Belt was still turning, just sluggish. Started noticing boards were dwelling too long in the preheat zones.
Noticed the conveyor on the line 4 unit wasn't keeping pace — speed gauge well below target but the belt wasn't dead. It's been off for at least half an hour according to the log.
Belt just froze mid-panel on line 1. Completely stopped, boards sitting there going nowhere. Nothing was moving at all — wasn't slow, wasn't sluggish, just dead stopped.
Walked over to the unit near the exit door and the whole conveyor was dead — zero movement. Could see the boards parked inside the tunnel, totally motionless. Hit the e-stop fast.
Line 2 oven alarm went off and when I got there the belt had stopped entirely. Not running slow — fully stopped. Boards just sitting in the hot zone.
Boards piling up at the front of the unit on line 3 — three of them stacked at the entry curtain. Won't feed in, just backing up at the load end.
Load side got backed up on second shift — panel boards stacking at the intake, nothing moving through the front gate. Entry sensor light was solid on the display.
Exit end is blocked on line 4 — boards coming out of the hot zone can't get through, bunching up at the unload curtain. Started noticing it halfway through second shift.
Boards are stacking at the cool end of the unit by the QC bench — can't come out. Exit sensor's been lit solid and I can see them piled up in there.
Advisory alarm came on the panel of the line 3 oven — exhaust flow is showing low but it's just the warning indicator, nothing critical. Still running, not smelling anything, just flagged it.
Airflow indicator dropped to the yellow zone on the display, production still going. Not shut down, no smell, just the advisory lamp. Probably the filter is getting dirty again.
Got a heads-up lamp on the line 1 oven panel for exhaust — flow reading is below the safe band but it's not an emergency level. We're still in production, need to get eyes on the filter.
Fan completely died on the unit near the back wall — exhaust reading was at zero and you could smell the flux vapors building up right away. Had to kill it immediately, second shift.
Exhaust went out entirely on line 2. The smell was bad — fumes hanging right over the machine. Airflow display was flatlined. Hit the estop fast and cleared the area.
N2 supply pressure alarm came on mid-run, reading was down from where it needs to be to keep the atmosphere right inside the tunnel. Worried about oxidation on the joints.
Nitrogen dropped during the afternoon batch on line 3. Pressure wasn't where it should be for the profile — had to check whether the cylinder bank was switching over correctly.
Boards coming off the exit on line 4 are way too hot to handle — picked one up and dropped it. Burned fingers. Cooling section isn't pulling the heat out properly.
Assembly coming out of the line 3 oven was warm enough to warp if you stacked them. Exit board temp was way high, not right at all.
Ground fault alarm lit up on the panel for zone 3 heater bank — never seen that one before. Killed power right away and called it in.
SCR fault showed up on the zone 2 heater bank display during first shift on line 1. Red indicator was on and the alarm was active.
Chain on the line 2 oven started making a dry squeaking noise during the run — checked the PM board and lubrication was due five days ago on this unit.
Maintenance schedule flagged the conveyor drive on the line 4 oven for lube — interval ran out, need to service it before the next production run.
Differential pressure gauge on the exhaust housing is in the red — filter's packed solid with flux residue, needs swapping out before it chokes off.
Filter change was flagged on the PM board for line 3 oven. Pressure drop across the filter is maxed out and it's starting to drag the airflow down.
Zone 2 TC was reading 3.5 degrees off when we ran it against the reference standard during the monthly check on line 1. Too much drift to leave it.
Calibration was due on zone 4 of the unit by the loading dock and the tech caught it drifting above tolerance during the scheduled verification. Had to log it.
Belt inspection came up on the PM schedule for line 1 — noticed some fraying at the edges of the wire mesh during the walkthrough. Needs to be logged and assessed.
Inspection due date came up for the line 3 unit and when we checked belt tension it was looser than spec — belt must have stretched over the last run cycle.
N2 flow reading on line 2 was jumping all over the place — not steady at all. Probably the sensor lens is dirty again, cleaning interval was past due.
Flow meter on the nitrogen line for the line 4 oven was erratic, bouncing up and down during the run. Cleaning was overdue per the PM sheet.
Noticed heavy flux deposits on the cooling fan blades during the PM walkthrough on line 3 — thick buildup, definitely restricting airflow in there.
Fan in the cooling section of the line 1 oven was making a grinding sound. Pulled the access panel and the blades were caked with flux residue.
Maintenance needed to get inside the tunnel on line 2 to swap out a heater rod. Had to do full energy isolation before anyone went in. All clear from safety before the work started.
Tech needed access to the interior of the line 4 oven to inspect the conveyor drive components. Couldn't start work until the full isolation was done and the physical lock was on.
Small flux drip on the side panel of the line 2 oven — maybe 300 milliliters, didn't spread far. Caught it early before it set. Just needs cleanup.
Found a little puddle of flux on the floor next to the unit by the QC bench — half a cup's worth at most, came from somewhere on the housing. Nothing major, clean it up.
Bit of flux got on the outer casing near the conveyor inlet on line 3 — small patch, under a liter for sure. Caught it early before it ran anywhere significant.
Whole two-liter flux jug tipped off the shelf above the line 1 oven and hit the floor — splattered everywhere under the machine and across the aisle. Fumes were immediate, had to clear the area.
Flux supply line blew a fitting near the line 3 oven and dumped probably six liters across the base of the unit and onto the floor. Strong fumes right away, had to stop everything and get people out.
Coming in on first shift Monday after the holiday weekend — oven on line 1 was completely off and stone cold. Needed to bring it all the way up from dead before we could run anything.
Line 4 oven had been shut down over the weekend maintenance window. First shift had to do the full cold restart procedure before production could start for the week.
